referents.why: 'from you' in Moses' continuing speech: the addressee, Pharaoh
feminine plural 'they will remain' agrees with the frogs (feminine plural)

links.why: then is within a verse only; cl4 is the last clause of the verse before (Exo.8.6), and this verse-initial weqatal has no earlier clause in its own verse. The join across the verse boundary is the episode rung

groups.why: Moses' speech continues from Exo.8.6 (Exo.8.6#turn1) into this verse: the frogs' departure and remaining are what Moses says. A turn cannot span verses, so this records this verse's clauses only, with the same sender and addressee

none_fit.what: an exception marked by רַק (only): the frogs depart, and they remain only in the Nile. As in Exo.8.5, no type covers an exception with רַק; contrast takes אוּלָם or אֶפֶס כִּי

cant_tell.what: whether the departure in cl0 (weqatal) is what the prayer brings about (a promised result), or only the continuation of Moses' speech
cant_tell.why: result is defined from an imperative; the prayer is not an imperative in this verse, and then does not cross verses
